*** SPRINT 73 / V0.29.28 -- US-549 (I-043) SHIPPED. 3 stories left: US-550 (I-044 XDG_RUNTIME_DIR %U), US-543 (A-4 parity guard, 6 assertions, M), US-545 (A-18 BT bond self-heal, M). ***\n\nUS-549 AS BUILT: shutdown-state-poll.js had FOUR terminal exits funnelling through one silent window.close(), so a correct abort and a cold-start race produced identical journals. Each exit now reports {cause, phase, reason, painted, elapsedMs, polls} on two sinks -- console (grep `[shutdown-splash] terminal`) and a zero-paint data-terminal-* attribute pair on <body>. `cause` is the SPLASH's business (why the render stopped); `phase`/`reason` are lifted verbatim off the last shutdown-state read (why the PI is going down). Two facts, both named. Never read a state file? phase/reason are null, NOT a plausible default -- that null IS the race evidence.\n\n*** THE LESSON FOR THE NEXT AGENT: A LOG LINE IS NOT AN OBSERVABLE UNTIL SOMETHING CARRIES IT. *** chromium DISCARDS web-content console output unless the unit passes --enable-logging=stderr. The JS half alone would have been a perfect, fully-tested, completely inert fix -- green suite, unchanged Pi. Both grace units now carry the flag. And the second trap inside that one: do NOT pin --log-level. Chromium logs web-content console messages at INFO REGARDLESS of the console method used (console.error does not become ERROR for ordinary page script), so --log-level=2 would have looked like a tasteful noise reduction and silently filtered out the only line the flag exists to surface. I nearly shipped exactly that.\n\nAC-vs-ISSUE TENSION, RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE ISSUE -- flagged, not silently narrowed: the AC says the splash should 'render' the reason. I-043's own text forbids a visible render ('forcing a paint when the state says the shutdown is over would be a dishonest instrument') and spec 6 requires cancelled/unrecognized to abort with no fadeout. So: journal + DOM attribute, no paint. Full reasoning in completionNotes; if Atlas/PM wants it visible that reverses an explicit US-525 decision and is a separate call.\n\n4 MUTATIONS, reverted by hand, byte-exact per `git diff --numstat` (wayland +14/-0, x11 +15/-1 = pure additions, no residue): (A) bare abort() -> 3 RED incl. the static no-silent-exit fence. (B) drop the logging flag from wayland -> 1 RED while x11 stayed GREEN, which ALSO proves the header comment mentioning the flag does not satisfy the guard (the US-501/US-513 prose trap -- reused test_dashboard_kit._execStartFlags and gave it a self-test with a positive control). (C) fabricate phase='cancelled' when nothing was read -> 1 RED. (D) collapse state-missing into cancelled -> 2 RED. (D) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the defect was never 'nothing is logged', it was 'the four outcomes are indistinguishable', so a single generic reason string would sail through a naive did-it-log test and leave I-043 fully open. Assert DISTINCTNESS, not presence.\n\nNEW INFRA you can reuse: tests/ui/shutdown_probe.js (node probe for the closeout splash -- the boot splash had one since US-499, the closeout had none, precisely because its only observable WAS window.close()) + runShutdownSplash() in render_harness.py. It CAPTURES console rather than silencing it, so tests assert the exact bytes the operator greps.\n\nGATE: 53 passed / EXIT 0 across the new file + the 4 neighbouring suites sharing these artifacts (ui/test_shutdown_splash_render, ui/test_splash_min_visible_floor, pi/splash/test_shutdown_splash_wiring, deploy/test_splash_kit). ruff clean on both .py files.\n\nENVIRONMENT (still true): `make` is NOT on PATH -- exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS. Use `python -m ruff check <file>`. pytest config SUPPRESSES the `N passed` line, so grepping for 'passed' returns NOTHING on a clean run -- trust the exit code. `rev` is not on this bash. Bash rejects `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` ('Contains expansion') -- run the plain command and read the tool's own exit report. Glob over the repo root TIMES OUT on this SMB share (20s) -- use `git ls-files | grep` instead, it is instant.\n\nSTILL OWED, Pi-side: the console->journal hop is the ONE link no headless test can prove. `journalctl -u splash-grace.service | grep '[shutdown-splash] terminal'` on the next clean shutdown, BEFORE spending a real AC-loss event on the reverse-splash drill. Prior sprint's F-126 debts + the I-us536 autoRotateS:0 resolver defect are unchanged and still open -- see offices/ralph/archive/ and the PM issues folder.\n\n--- PRIOR SESSION (Sprint 71) NOTE FOLLOWS, still relevant for F-126 debts ---\n\n*** SPRINT 71 / V0.29.26 IS COMPLETE -- 7/7, US-548 landed this iteration. BUT DO NOT DEPLOY ON THAT GREEN ALONE: US-548 uncovered a HIGH-severity defect that makes US-536's freeze fix AND US-533's auto-rotate toggle INERT. Read the next paragraph before anything else. ***

THE FINDING. config.json ships pi.display.carousel.autoRotateS: 0 (US-536 AC-2, the durable freeze fix). resolveCarouselConfig REJECTS it -- carousel.js:218 admits an injected override only when `v > 0` -- so 0 falls back to CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS.autoRotateS = 8 and the carousel keeps rotating. Repo-visible end to end: carousel.js:2858 resolves DISPLAY_CAROUSEL -> :3693 feeds shouldAutoAdvance -> :230 advances on 8. US-533's toggle is hit by the SAME line: settingsWriteValue (carousel.js:1272) writes exactly 0 for 'Off', the overlay stores 0, the endpoint honestly re-reads 0, the band repaints 'Off' -- and nothing changes. Every layer is individually honest; only the consumer disagrees. That is the exact silent no-op the F-126 band was built to prevent, and it slipped through precisely BECAUSE no layer lied. Filed I-us536-shipped-autorotates-zero-is-rejected-by-resolver.md (HIGH, 3 options + a recommendation). NOT fixed by me: carousel.js is outside US-548's fence, and the fix means choosing between two DELIBERATE invariants -- US-506 rejects 0 so a MISCONFIG cannot silently kill the carousel, US-536 uses 0 to DELIBERATELY kill it. Same value, opposite meanings; that is an architecture call. It also undercuts US-537's still-owed AllocateRingBuffer drill, whose whole premise is auto-rotate being off, and it means V0.29.26 currently ships the GPU ON with its compensating control inert.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, BECAUSE THE METHOD GENERALISES: I-us536 suggested fixing the third red by repointing _AUTO_ROTATE_S to 0. I CHECKED the suggestion instead of applying it, and that one check surfaced everything. That constant carried THREE facts and US-536 moved only one: (a) carousel.js's CAROUSEL_DEFAULTS fallback -- still 8; (b) an arbitrary SAMPLE INTERVAL for six shouldAutoAdvance/rotateProgress assertions, where a non-positive value means 'disabled' and cannot stand in for a period; (c) config.json's shipped default -- now 0. Repointing the name would have been wrong in 8 of its 9 uses AND would have shipped a green suite over the dead fix. I added a separate _SHIPPED_AUTO_ROTATE_S = 0 for (c) only. A HANDED-DOWN DISPOSITION IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN INSTRUCTION -- and the issue's own 'worth checking whether the same constant feeds other assertions' caveat turned out to be the whole story.

*** THE LESSON I MOST WANT THE NEXT AGENT TO HAVE: INVERTING A GUARD DESTROYS ITS SAFETY NET. *** While a guard asserts PRESENCE, a rotted parser fails LOUDLY -- an empty token list cannot contain the flag. Asserting ABSENCE, the identical rotted parser passes VACUOUSLY. Not theory: Mutation C (make _execStartFlags return []) -> 5 RED, and my headline guard test_dashboardUnits_keepTheGpuOn_us536 STAYED GREEN. The whole story's main assertion was vacuous under a dead parser. So I added a POSITIVE CONTROL to the parser self-test (it must still FIND --disable-gpu when the flag genuinely is on an ExecStart); that is what caught Mutation C. Any future presence->absence inversion needs the same treatment.

AND THE SUBSTRING TRAP INVERTS WITH IT, which is why 'do not weaken to substring checks' matters in a NEW direction: under a PRESENCE check a naive `'--disable-gpu' in text` accepts the narrower --disable-gpu-rasterization as the fix (false NEGATIVE); under an ABSENCE check it REJECTS a unit legitimately carrying that flag (false POSITIVE). Mutation B planted --disable-gpu-rasterization on the REAL wayland unit -> stayed GREEN, correctly. Also: both units STILL carry US-522 comments discussing --disable-gpu, so the parser's comment-stripping is now load-bearing against a false positive rather than a false negative.

US-548 AS BUILT: 2 guards inverted + renamed to us536 (keepTheGpuOn; keyringFixSurvivedTheGpuRevert -- keyring half untouched per AC-3, and the risk that fence NOW guards is a GPU-aimed revert taking --password-store=basic with it, since they are adjacent lines in one continuation block). _GPU_OVERRIDE_FLAG -> _GPU_DISABLE_FLAG. US-522's RCA history KEPT in the header (it is what makes the inverted assertion legible) with disposition B's reasoning added. Third red fixed via the new constant, and its docstring now states plainly that it pins WHAT CONFIG.JSON CONTAINS and does NOT prove the display honours it -- so the green cannot be misread. Declaration-vs-mechanism, five sprints running.

5 MUTATIONS, all reverted BY HAND (git checkout is outside the allow-list), reverts confirmed byte-exact via `git diff --numstat` showing NEITHER unit file in the diff: (A) re-add --disable-gpu -> 2 RED, exactly the inverted guards. (B) plant the narrower flag -> GREEN, correctly. (C) parser returns [] -> 5 RED via the new positive control. (D) drop --password-store=basic -> 2 RED incl. my renamed fence. (E) repoint _SHIPPED_AUTO_ROTATE_S -> 1 RED against the real config.json. NO RED-FIRST CLAIM IS MADE OR NEEDED: the 3 tests were ALREADY RED at session start (reproduced before touching anything). My edits go red->green, so the burden is the REVERSE -- prove the green is not vacuous. Mutation C proves that burden was real.

GATE: targeted = the 2 changed files, 98 passed, exit 0, re-run green after all 5 reverts; ruff clean on both. AC-4 asks for the FULL SUITE, which prompt.md forbids in-loop (TD-059), so I ran the two DIRECTORIES I touched -- `tests/deploy/ tests/ui/` -- EXIT CODE 0, no FAILED/ERROR. FOR PM: the full-suite half of AC-4 is yours at integration. All 3 known reds are now retired, so that gate is finally meaningful; my diff is test-only + 2 new PM docs and touches no src/, but US-533's three changed call signatures on the Pi hot path are what the full suite is actually for.

ALSO FILED: TD-078 -- both dashboard units still carry multi-paragraph comments arguing FOR --disable-gpu (x11 19-45, wayland 24-39), including a live-verification claim now false of what deploys. Harmless at runtime, but the next freeze investigation will read exactly that file and find a confident case to re-add the flag, with nothing recording that the CIO rejected it. US-536's lane.

STILL OWED FOR F-126 (unchanged, Pi-side, nothing on the dev box can close these): auto-rotate toggle -> UI reload -> carousel picks up the new period with NO states-http restart; power mode -> wall -> tile follows within one emit cycle; reboot -> both survive via the overlay; plus US-537's AllocateRingBuffer drill with auto-rotate ON. THE FIRST AND LAST ARE NOW GATED ON THE NEW ISSUE -- with autoRotateS:0 rejected, 'auto-rotate off' cannot currently be observed on the Pi at all.

ENVIRONMENT: `make` is NOT on PATH (exits 127, WHICH READS LIKE A PASS) -- use `python -m ruff check` per file; TD-075 keeps project-wide ruff at exit 1. This repo's pytest config SUPPRESSES the `N passed` line, so grepping for 'passed' returns NOTHING on a CLEAN run -- confirm via exit code, never an empty grep. NEW: `tests/deploy/ tests/ui/` together exceed even a 600s Bash timeout on this SMB share and got backgrounded (the TD-059 trap) -- I recovered it by reading the completed output file IN-ITERATION rather than losing the result. Tool syntax, all hit this session: PowerShell rejected both an expandable string carrying $LASTEXITCODE and $() subexpressions; Bash rejected a `for f in ...; do` loop, multi-operation && chains, and a python heredoc containing quotes. When both shells refuse, run ONE plain command and use the tool's own exit reporting, or write the file with the Write tool.
